response.sql: WITH per_id AS (SELECT ID, AVG(ANA) AS avg_ana FROM Examination WHERE ID IS NOT NULL GROUP BY ID HAVING AVG(ANA) IS NOT NULL), m AS (SELECT AVG(avg_ana) AS mean_avg FROM per_id) SELECT p.ID, p.avg_ana, p.avg_ana - m.mean_avg AS gap_above_mean FROM per_id p CROSS JOIN m WHERE p.avg_ana > m.mean_avg ORDER BY gap_above_mean DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: IDs whose ANA values are all NULL have no per-ID average and are excluded from both the list and the mean of per-ID averages; AVG ignores NULL ANA values within an ID.
The mean of all per-ID averages is an unweighted mean across IDs (each ID counts once), not the overall average of ANA across all rows.
Rows with NULL ID are ignored because they cannot be attributed to a patient.
Missing-last ordering is moot since only IDs with a non-null average above the mean are returned, so gaps are never NULL.
